title: The loop that knows when to stop

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model.

tasks.title: Run every call in a reply
tasks.description:
Implement `runToolCalls(calls)` in `src/agent.ts`.

It receives the `tool_calls` of one assistant message. For each call, look up the function by name in `toolFunctions` (from `src/tools.ts`), run it with the parsed arguments, and build a tool message:

```ts
{ role: 'tool', tool_call_id: call.id, content: JSON.stringify(result) }
```

Return the messages in the same order as the calls. An empty list gives an empty array. An error object returned by a tool, such as an unknown order, is a normal result. For now you can assume the model only asks for tools that exist.
nextSteps: Read `toolFunctions` in `src/tools.ts`: it maps a tool name to a function.
Map over the calls and parse each call's arguments.
Run the function and wrap its result in a tool message.
hints: This is the same tool message you built by hand in the last issue, once per call.
Check `call.type === 'function'` before you read `call.function`. A `filter` before the `map` keeps TypeScript happy.
`toolFunctions[call.function.name](JSON.parse(call.function.arguments))` gives you the result to stringify.

tasks.title: Keep going until there is an answer
tasks.description:
Implement `runAgent(question, options?)` in `src/agent.ts`.

Start the conversation with `SYSTEM` and the question. Then repeat:

1. Send the whole conversation to `MODEL` with `tools: toolSpecs`.
2. If the reply has no tool calls, you are done.
3. Otherwise append the assistant message and the tool messages from `runToolCalls`, and go again.

Return `{ answer, steps }`: the content of the final reply and the number of model requests made. Use `options.client` when it is given. The check asks questions that need one, two and three tool calls, and runs a scripted model to see that each request carries the whole conversation.
nextSteps: Build the messages array once, before the loop.
Inside a loop, make the request and look at the reply's `tool_calls`.
Return when there are none; otherwise append and loop again.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and check the step count.
hints: One question can need several rounds: the model looks up the order first, then each product in it.
Count requests as you make them, not tool calls. A reply with tool calls and the final reply are both steps.
The loop body is the round trip from the last issue: push `reply`, then spread `runToolCalls(reply.tool_calls)` into the same array.

tasks.title: Stop a run that would never end
tasks.description:
Some requests never finish. Ask Pip to wait until order PL-2047 is delivered and the model will check the order again and again, because nothing in this run changes it.

Give `runAgent` a step limit: `options.maxSteps`, default `6`. If the model still wants tools after `maxSteps` requests, throw `new StepLimitError(maxSteps)` (already defined in `src/agent.ts`).

The check runs a model that never stops and expects exactly `maxSteps` requests, then the error. It also makes sure an answer that arrives on the last allowed request is still returned.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and watch the second question.
Throw `StepLimitError` after the loop ends without an answer.
Test the edge: an answer on request number `maxSteps` must still win.
hints: A `for` loop with a counter is easier to reason about here than `while (true)`.
The error belongs after the loop, not inside it: you only reach that line when every allowed step asked for tools.
Count from 1 and keep going while `step <= maxSteps`. Then the request numbered `maxSteps` still runs.
